patients with advanced disease, especially those with extensive pulmonary metastases, have a poor prognosis, while those presenting with minimal to moderate disease, regardless of the extent or location of disease, have a good prognosis.

the combination of extensive pulmonary metastases with extensive retroperitoneal metastases and/or liver involvement is associated with a very poor prognosis, with a high incidence of tumor recurrence after achieving remission and a low incidence of sustained remission.

patients with stage B3 disease or stage B2 disease with minimal to moderate associated pulmonary disease have an excellent chance of cure with a combination of chemotherapy and surgical removal of the residual disease.
the extent of disease is more important than the histology or type of chemotherapy employed in predicting survival.

1) preoperative combination chemotherapy with cisplatin is superior to other chemotherapy regimens for advanced disease, 2) the extent of pulmonary metastases is the most important prognostic factor, 3) the presence of massive abdominal disease is not a contraindication to surgical resection and 4) the presence of liver metastases in the absence of massive abdominal and/or pulmonary disease is not a significant contraindication for surgical resection.
